assumptions: 1. THE CREATORS DECLARE NOTHING YET (VELDO-0302 is not built). The suite declares and confirms each run directory, scratch folder, worktree and clone item itself, the clone's three items owned by the worker dispatch's run. In production nothing records them yet, so a receiver's space end finds no item and sends nothing.

2. NOTHING IN THE ENGINE BUILDS `space` YET. The receiver's main() passes none and no Runner is given one, so until a later ticket wires it every path here runs as before: the run directory goes where it went, no hold is released, no retry is made, the clone obligation closes when the files are gone. The suite wires the mapping itself.

3. NOTHING WRITES A HOLD YET (VELDO-0316: the Runner's hold, the contract's space field, the freed mark and the space wake). The suite places and admits each hold through the ledger's own commands and judges the waiting unit with control_space_admission.admit. The receiver releases the hold the contract's space field names, else the one under the dispatch's identity; the freed mark and the wake that 6.7 says the release raises are VELDO-0334 and are not here.

4. THE OWNER'S CONFIRM IS NOT BUILT (VELDO-0320). In ac4/pins-follow-the-removal it stands as what it will make: a removal of the deferred items through Signal, sent from outside the teardown and the retirement, after the slot was released.

5. THE RECEIVER, THE RUNNER AND THE CLONE PROVISIONER ARE MADE WITHOUT THEIR STORES (object.__new__ and the attributes the driven paths read). Receiver.launch is driven on two of its refusal paths since the fix round (f5/refused-before-spawn, f5/spawn-failed), with the stations before the spawn standing in (the recheck, the qualification, the login, the binding, the memory handoff answer that nothing is wrong) and a spawn that raises as a missing program does; its other refusal paths call the space end in the same place and are read, not driven. Receiver._finish is driven with recording stand-ins for the dispatch records and the emit. The reservation service is a stand-in as far as a retirement reads it; the real one is exercised with the changed retirement module by suites 63 and 67, which are green. The dispatch records the start sweep reads are a table of two rows.

6. OTHER STAND-INS. The row VELDO-0347 adds to the kind registry (an agent repository at run finished: remove), on a copy. The two checks of a switch to act (VELDO-0332, 0339). The docker client (a function). The process table (a fixture folder shaped as the kernel's; in ac1/surviving-child its entry is that of a real child process that really holds the file, and the row reads the real /proc of that child to show it). The group's emptiness is the receiver's supervision as its reap leaves it, set by the row; no systemd scope is made.

7. THE PINS ARE FOLLOWED FROM DISK (fix round, review finding 4). follow_pins reads the pin refs in the caches at each call and keeps nothing in memory, so a restart forgets no pin. It releases only when the ledger records an item at the work tree's path, every item there is removed or gone, and nothing is at the path. A work tree no item ever recorded is never released by it: such a pin stays until the provisioner's own teardown releases it. A held pin keeps objects and loses nothing.

8. A SWEEP IS NO RETRY (fix round, review finding 1, the lead's decision). Runner.clear_runs sends run finished only while no ending event has reached the run directory's item, at most once, and for the run directory alone; a held item is dropped as handed over. Until VELDO-0315 or 0316 lands, a deferred run directory of a run whose outcome is unknown (no retirement completes) stays on disk until reconcile. That costs space and loses nothing.

9. NARROWER THAN THE AMENDMENT'S WORDS, ON THE SAFE SIDE. The clone obligation closes on a space_deferred refusal only while the ledger records the clone's root as a live item in state due, deferred, removing or kept. A clone no item records, a root the event never reached, and an unreadable ledger keep the slot held. Recorded for the lead in the spec's History.

10. THE DESIGN'S RETRY PARAGRAPH (section 7) and the Retirement row of its component table still carry the wording from before AC4; the design is outside this footprint and is to be revised by the lead.

11. ALONE IS THE LIMIT USED. The ledger's signal takes an owner and no single item, and the ledger module is outside this footprint, so the sweep and the receiver send with `alone` and look first: while the run's owner also has a live worktree or agent repository that is not at or beneath the run's folders, nothing is sent (not_alone). For a clone its teardown sends the one event for that owner. A run that owned such an item which no teardown ends would be sent nothing by its receiver until that item's own event or reconcile; nothing declares one that way today (VELDO-0302 decides the owners). Recorded for the lead in the spec's History. SINCE FIX ROUND 2 (N1) the look counts only items of a clone of the same owner (beneath the clones folder, in a state an event takes): a run that owns a worktree or agent repository that is no clone's is sent run finished, and that event ends it.

12. THE HOLD OF A RUN WHOSE GROUP WAS UNREAD STAYS HELD (fix round, review finding 3). The receiver keeps it, the sweep removes the folders once the kernel shows the run gone, and nothing but the receiver releases a hold in this ticket: it stays until VELDO-0315 or 0316 gives the sweep or reconcile that release, as for an unknown outcome.

13. THE FIX ROUND'S FALSIFIERS WERE APPLIED TO THE REPOSITORY COPY, NOT THROUGH THE OBSERVER. Each was written into .veldo/<module>, the suite run with a stub engine, and the copy put back from engine/.veldo and compared byte for byte. The launch cases were applied twice (the second time to record what each row said) and the pin cases three times (once more after the pin listing was moved to git_process); every application was red on its target rows. The stability figure of finding 2 (0 of 200) is from this host, idle but for the run itself.

14. ITEMS BEHIND A HANDED-OVER, DEFERRED CLONE WAIT FOR THE LEDGER'S NEXT RETRY, AND NOTHING IN PRODUCTION MAKES ONE FOR THEM TODAY (fix round 2, the re-review's finding 1). space_retry has one production caller, Retirements._attempt, for a retirement that was pending and is released; a retirement that hands the clone over and releases in the same attempt never calls it. The run's own items the teardown's event did not reach then stay present, sent nothing (not_alone), until admission (VELDO-0316) or reconcile (VELDO-0315) is built, or the signal that names items lets run finished be sent for them beside the clone. Nothing is ended wrongly and nothing is lost; it costs space without bound in that case. The creators of VELDO-0302 that declare run items beside a clone depend on it. Recorded for the lead in the spec's History; the row asserts the items stay deferred and unharmed over five production sweeps.

15. THE BUNDLE CITES 8074ab92, THE COMMIT OF THE ENGINE CHANGE OF FIX ROUND 2. The suite row n1/handed-over-clone-untouched and the N1 History were corrected after it, in commit 03172b82, which changes no engine file; the suite figures and the four falsifier applications of this round are from that tree.
rollback: Revert the change. The receiver sends no run finished, and the run's items stay present until another event ends them.
